Official answer explicitly Not solved. Part d asks elementary forms; second independent solution is a quadrature involving integral exp(s²), not an elementary function. Explain infeasible demand, provide convergent series and exact quadrature.
Original sum starts at n=0 but coefficient 1/(n 2^n) is undefined there. Preserve problem with explicit deletion of undefined zero term; convergence radius of positive terms unchanged.
Original m,c,k>0 conflicts with b.i c=0. Preserve both; treat b.i as undamped boundary case.
Original complex-root graphing instruction calls shape spiral; pure imaginary roots here yield a center and closed ellipses. Explained from invariant.
Decreasing must be strict, or positive/negative signs on two sides of a required. Nonincreasing alone does not imply isolated limit cycle.
Orthogonality formula diagonal value pi assumes positive integer indices; m=n=0 exception 2pi stated.
